title_guess: How HDI is calculated: dimensions, indicators, goalposts, normalisation, geometric mean, and India's values and rank
recurring_cast: HDI title with a '3 Dimensions' tag
blue dimension bar: standard of living | health | education
range_bar (a 0 to 1 bar under min and max; later with a small cap drawn over it)
country_flag (Bulgaria for the made-up example, India for real values)
goalpost table_grid: dimension, indicator, min, max, then actual value and index value columns
formula box: index = (actual - min) / (max - min), later swapped for the log version
green highlight frame on the row being worked
running_examples: made-up 'Bulgaria' indices 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 -> HDI = cube root of (0.7 x 0.8 x 0.9) = 0.795
goalposts shown: GNP per capita PPP $100 to $75,000; life expectancy 20 to 85 years; expected years of schooling 0 to 18; mean years of schooling 0 to 15
India education: 11.9 -> x, 6.7 -> y, index = (x + y) / 2 (x and y never computed)
India income: log 6590 - log 100 over log 75000 - log 100 (result never shown; only a tick)
India HDI 0.633, medium human development band (0.550 to 0.700), rank 132 of 191

best_moments.why: under each indicator's min and max arrows a short 0-to-1 bar pops in, one per indicator on the beat of '0 se 1 ke beech': normalisation shown as the same ruler under every indicator
three arrows run from the 0.7, 0.8 and 0.9 cells into one 'geometric mean' label, which then becomes 'HDI =' with the product under a cube root: three numbers visibly merge into one
after the first answer, the indicator row and the min/max row turn yellow with a big '?' at the end of each: the open questions for the rest of the video are marked on the picture itself

worked row method: a green frame locks onto the health row, the actual value 67.2 years is written beside it, the general formula box is filled with that row's own numbers and the answer 0.726 lands in the index column
a curly brace joins the two education results (x, y) and an arrow leads to (x + y) / 2: two indicators visibly folded into one index
a red cross stamps the linear formula box when it 'will not work' for income, and a log version replaces it: a rule change shown on the rule itself
India's 0.633 card sends an arrow into the 'medium' row of a four-band table, then the rank '132 out of 191' writes under it: a score placed on its scale

weak_moments.why: the example indices 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 are 'maan lijiye' numbers but are pinned to a real country's flag; BIE should use a made-up country or real data, not both

the goalpost stretch (about 100 s) is a text table filled cell by cell; the long spoken rule (below min -> 0, above max -> 1, in between -> calculated) is shown only by a small cap over the 0-1 bar, never by a value being clamped
three indicator definitions as English callout paragraphs on a dimmed canvas (about 45 s); no picture of a newborn, a school or an adult's schooling years
education index is left as x and y; the numbers 11.9/18 and 6.7/15 are never worked, so the learner never sees an education index value
the income index is written as a log fraction and then only a tick; its value (about 0.63) is never shown, and why logs are needed (each extra dollar matters less at high incomes) is never said
the four band cut-offs (0.800, 0.700, 0.550) are on screen but never spoken
check before reuse: the screen and voice say 'GNP per capita'; the UNDP report uses GNI per capita (2017 PPP $). Goalposts and India figures match one HDR edition and should be dated

segments.teaches: recall: growth is measured by GDP, GNP, NNP, NDP and per capita income; development (quality of life) needs HDI

'economic growth' (green) and 'economic development - quality of life' (blue), split by a dotted line
list GDP, GNP, NNP, NDP, per capita income under growth
'HDI' in purple under development

segments.notes: Opening already built when the first keyframe is taken; recall of the previous video while the voice says the same.
segments.idea: growth and development are measured differently; development is measured by HDI
segments.shown_as: two halves split by a dotted line, each topped by a measuring tape: the growth half lists five income measures, the development half carries only the purple word HDI

segments.teaches: HDI has three dimensions (standard of living, health, education); each is measured by an indicator with a minimum and maximum; each value is normalised to between 0 and 1

elements.what: HDI with a pink '3 Dimensions' tag
blue bar with three dimension chips
a line drops from each chip to an 'Indicator' label, which forks into Min and Max arrows
short 0-to-1 bar under each Min/Max pair

segments.notes: 8 change events in 36 s. The three 0-1 bars pop in one by one (36.2, 37.4, 38.6) on the single phrase '0 se lekar 1 ke beech'.
segments.idea: each of three dimensions is read from an indicator, which is squeezed onto the same 0 to 1 scale
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to an HDI title; a '3 Dimensions' tag and a blue bar with three chips appear; a line drops from each chip to an 'Indicator' label that forks into Min and Max arrows, and a short 0-to-1 bar pops under each pair, left to right

segments.teaches: worked example: if a country's three indices are 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, HDI is their geometric mean, the cube root of their product, 0.795

elements.what: grey row with a Bulgaria flag and three cells under the three dimensions
cells fill 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 one by one
three purple arrows converge on a 'geometric mean' label
HDI = cube root (0.7 x 0.8 x 0.9) = 0.795

segments.notes: 7 change events; the three values are too small for the event detector (seen in keyframes 59.7 and 69.7). The 'geometric mean' label is swapped for 'HDI =' and the formula writes on piece by piece with the voice (product, then root).
segments.idea: HDI = cube root of (health x education x income index)
segments.shown_as: a grey row with a flag slides under the tree and its three cells fill 0.7, 0.8, 0.9; three purple arrows converge from the cells onto 'geometric mean'; the label turns into 'HDI =', the three numbers are written with x signs, a cube-root sign draws over them and '= 0.795' appears

segments.teaches: open questions: what are the real indicators, and what are their real minimum and maximum values (0 and 1 are only the scaled ends)

elements.what: yellow band over the three Indicator labels, '?' at its end
yellow band over the Min/Max row, '?' at its end
two '?' marks

segments.notes: 2 change events. A cheap, effective agenda device: the unknown parts are lit and questioned on the existing picture.
segments.idea: the example skipped two things that must now be learned: the indicators and their goalposts
segments.shown_as: the indicator row and then the min/max row are each covered by a yellow band ending in a big question mark, while the finished HDI formula stays below

segments.teaches: the goalposts: GNP per capita in PPP dollars 100 to 75,000; life expectancy 20 to 85 years; expected years of schooling 0 to 18; mean years of schooling 0 to 15; values below the minimum count as 0 and above the maximum as 1

elements.what: rows = three dimension chips, columns = indicator, Min, Max; header shows the 0-1 bar over Min and Max
indicator names written into the cells
min and max numbers fill cell by cell
small cap/cage drawn over the 0-1 header bar (values boxed between 0 and 1)

segments.notes: 6 change events in about 100 s (~every 16 s), mostly small cell writes. The tree reshapes into a table. The long spoken clamping rule (about 30 s) gets only the small cap over the header bar.
segments.idea: each indicator has a fixed lowest and highest value used to scale it
segments.shown_as: the tree reshapes into a table: dimension chips down the left, an indicator column, and Min/Max columns under the 0-1 bar; indicator names and their min and max numbers are written in row by row, and a small cap is drawn over the 0-1 bar when the voice says no value can go below 0 or above 1

segments.teaches: meanings: life expectancy at birth (years a newborn can expect to live at current death rates); expected years of schooling (years a school-age child can expect to get); mean years of schooling (average years of education of people aged 25 and older)

elements.what: canvas dims; one indicator cell at a time lit in blue
blue definition box beside the lit cell, in English

segments.notes: 6 change events. Spotlight-and-callout pattern; content is three English sentences on screen while the voice explains in Hindi.
segments.idea: what each of the three non-income indicators actually counts
segments.shown_as: the whole table dims; the life-expectancy cell lights blue and a definition box pops beside it; the light then jumps to expected years and then to mean years of schooling, each with its own box
segments.example: mean years counts people aged 25 and older

segments.teaches: India's health index = (67.2 - 20) / (85 - 20) = 0.726; education: expected 11.9 and mean 6.7 years give x and y by the same formula, and the education index is (x + y) / 2

elements.what: India flag over a new 'Actual Value' column, then an 'Index Value' column
green frame on the health row
blue box: index value = (actual - min) / (max - min), filled as (67.2 - 20) / (85 - 20) = 0.726
67.2 years, 0.726, 11.9, 6.7 written into columns
11.9 -> x, 6.7 -> y; curly brace -> (x + y) / 2
dark frame around the formula box when it is reused

segments.notes: 8 change events in 82 s. The 0.726 is carried from the formula into the table cell. x and y are never given numbers.
segments.idea: an index is how far the actual value has moved from the minimum toward the maximum
segments.shown_as: the table brightens; an India flag heads a new actual-value column; a green frame locks onto the health row, 67.2 years is written beside it, and a formula box below fills with that row's own min and max to give 0.726, which also lands in a new index column; 11.9 and 6.7 are written for education, each arrows to x and y, and a curly brace joins them into (x + y) / 2

segments.teaches: income uses logs: (log 6590 - log 100) / (log 75000 - log 100); the geometric mean of the three indices gives India's HDI, 0.633

elements.what: 6590 written in the income row, with an arrow to a tick in the index column
red cross on the linear formula box
box swapped for: log actual - log min over log max - log min; filled with 6590, 100, 75000
purple band down the index column, labelled 'geometric mean', arrow to HDI
HDI 0.633 under the arrow

segments.notes: 6 change events. The income index value is never shown; a tick stands in for it.
segments.idea: income is scaled on a log scale, then the three indices combine into one HDI
segments.shown_as: 6590 is written in the income row with an arrow to a tick; a red cross lands on the linear formula box and it is replaced by a log version, whose numerator and denominator fill with 6590, 100 and 75000; the index column is banded purple, labelled geometric mean, and an arrow drops to HDI 0.633

segments.teaches: UNDP puts countries in four HDI groups; India's 0.633 is 'medium'; India ranks 132 of 191
